answer:
RESULT — full PCA executed on the 12 Z-capital variables (39 × 100-yr bins).

CORE FINDING
PC1 explains 30.3% of the variance and is a composite capital-accumulation axis (positive loadings: ZCU_AU +0.41, Zkeverz +0.38, ZHort +0.34, ZAxtSchwert +0.30, ZDolch +0.27, ZMW +0.24, Zhausgr +0.23, ZMonument +0.20; negative: ZKeform −0.35, ZBeil −0.24, Zamber −0.24, ZSichel −0.15). Because PC1 scores are centered, the full-series mean is 0.0.

Both target phases sit on the LOW (negative) end of PC1 — every one of their 12 bins falls below the 0.0 series mean.

Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE, group MN, 5 bins):
  3400: PC1 −0.583 (rank 21)
  3300: PC1 −1.280 (rank 15)
  3200: PC1 −1.757 (rank 10)
  3100: PC1 −1.467 (rank 13)
  3000: PC1 −1.783 (rank 6, series low)
  Mean PC1 ≈ −1.37 (i.e. 1.37 below the full-series mean). Trend: a FALLING segment as time advances 3400→3000, reaching its minimum (rank ~6 of 39) at 3000 BCE.

Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE, group SG, 7 bins):
  2900: −1.504 (rank 12)
  2800: −1.599 (rank 11)
  2700: −0.683 (rank 19)
  2600: −1.116 (rank 17)
  2500: −1.214 (rank 16)
  2400: −1.293 (rank 14)
  2300: −0.412 (rank 22)
  Mean PC1 ≈ −1.12. Trend: essentially FLAT/noisy (range −0.41 to −1.60) with a mild recovery toward 2300 BCE.

CHARACTERIZATION (the requested triad)
- Level: both phases are strongly negative on PC1 → low aggregate capital accumulation relative to the whole Neolithic–Bronze-Age sequence.
- Trend: MN is a declining segment bottoming out at 3000 BCE; YN is low and roughly stable with a slight uptick at 2300 BCE.
- Relative position: all 12 bins are in the lower half of the 39-bin distribution (ranks 6–22); the positive/high-capital part of the series lies later (post-Neolithic).

SECONDARY POLLIN CONTEXT (Belau openness, SMOOTH_MEAN_100y, calBP=BCE+1950)
- MN (calBP 4950–5350): openness falls from ≈ +0.20 (3400 BCE) to ≈ −1.81 (3000 BCE) — a closing/less-open landscape, consistent with the capital trough.
- YN (calBP 4250–4850): openness stays low and roughly flat (≈ −0.40 to −0.75).
This is a separate proxy and is offered only as corroborating context, not part of the capital PCA.

HYPOTHESIS (natural-language answer)
In the PCA on the 12 forms of capital analyzed in 100-year time slices, PC1 (≈30% variance) captures an axis of aggregate capital accumulation. Both the Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE) and the Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE) are characterized by strongly negative PC1 scores, i.e. low capital accumulation relative to the full series: the Middle Neolithic is a declining segment that bottoms out at 3000 BCE (PC1 ≈ −1.78, the series low), while the Younger Neolithic remains low and broadly stable (mean ≈ −1.12, a slight recovery by 2300 BCE). Pollen openness at Belau (secondary) declines through the Middle Neolithic and stays low through the Younger Neolithic, consistent with a low-accumulation, less-open landscape in both phases.

payload.workflow: Load capital.csv; drop group & color; convert comma-decimal strings to float on the 12 Z-columns; re-standardize (mean 0, unit variance); run PCA via SVD on the 39×12 matrix; extract PC1 scores per 100-yr bin; characterize MN (3400–3000) and SG/YN (2900–2300) by mean level, within-window trend, and rank/position vs the full series; cross-check with Belau pollen SMOOTH_MEAN_100y aligned via calBP=BCE+1950.
